chapter: New Orleans clarinetists and learning the guitar
title: Big Eye Louis, the Barquets and a clarinetist who crossed over
summary: Asked about Louis Nelson's father; Keppard recalls a clarinetist who passed into white bands for more money, was found out and left for Chicago and California.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. The only word must have been worse at that time. It's his voice. Do you remember, if I remember rightly, Big Eye Louie, you know, Louie Nelson, the clarinet player, I think said his father was killed in that riot. Do you remember? Did he ever tell you anything about it? Well, I didn't know Louie's father, whatever. I didn't know him. I don't know what. I mean, did Louie ever tell you anything about it?

No. He never said nothing about it. The only thing I've been knowing Louie for a couple of years, and I see a barque and George Barque, and I knew it was all them barqueers. One of them used to play a lot of bands, you know, on the other side. Yeah. Of course, I understand he's right between lines on the other side. Yeah. And, of course, I played with him. I think he's dead now, too.
John's dead. John's dead. And Ashiel's dead. But, of course, Ashiel was a clarinet player. He was tough.
Did you ever work with him, too?

Oh, yeah, I worked with him. I did. Before you left him. I worked with him, and then after that, he crossed over. Yeah. Well, then they got some of the white boys. They liked the way he played, heard him, and they knew he was a clarinet player, and they just used him. Yeah. Then after that, they used him a couple of times, and he stuck.
Well, after he stuck, well, he forgot about the other fellow, what he used to be with.
Well, of course, I understand. I don't blame him. Of course, there was more money. There was more money in that than with us.
He wanted that. See? I couldn't blame him, I guess.

Then what happened to him is he went too far, I guess. And the wildestad, that he takes and went and started fooling around, fooling around. After he got so bright on clarinet, and so perfect on a clarinet, and making the baby cry, and all that, and the other fellows were having a good time. So he figured he'd have a good time. And after that, they found him out that they said, when we called for a white band, we want some white band. We don't want a colored band. So that would knock him out. So after you're knocking him out there, well, I see, well, he had to take and leave. Or they went to Chicago or somewhere.
I think you met Los Angeles finally. He died out there.

Exactly. But I know that's the trouble today, that they found it out. They was colored, and they know it all the time. But as long as he was in his place, he was solid. But the minute that he overcome his jurisdiction, then he takes and he fell down. Like the old words say, who fell down, stayed down. So he went down. And he had to get out of the band. Then he takes and go to California somewhere, as I don't exactly know. But I knew he hurt his own self in the band. So any other thing, Mr.
